title: Shopping for records
description: Natural beginner phrases for browsing a record shop, asking about music, finding vinyl, discussing condition and price, and buying records.

lessons.english: Hi, I'm looking for some records.
acceptedTranslations: Hello, I'm looking for some records.
Hi, I'm looking for a few records.
notes: « Estoy buscando... » is an extremely useful construction when shopping.

lessons.english: Are you looking for anything in particular?
acceptedTranslations: Are you looking for something specific?
Looking for anything in particular?
notes: A natural question from someone working in a shop.

lessons.sentence: Sí, busco música de los setenta.
lessons.english: Yes, I'm looking for music from the seventies.
acceptedTranslations: Yes, I'm looking for seventies music.
Yes, I'm looking for music from the 1970s.
notes: « Los setenta » means the seventies.

lessons.english: What kind of music do you like?
acceptedTranslations: What type of music do you like?
What kind of music are you into?
notes: A broadly useful question for talking about musical tastes.

lessons.sentence: Me gusta mucho el rock clásico.
lessons.english: I really like classic rock.
acceptedTranslations: I like classic rock a lot.
I'm really into classic rock.
notes: « Me gusta mucho... » is a basic, high-value way to express preferences.

lessons.english: Do you have any David Bowie records?
acceptedTranslations: Do you have David Bowie records?
Do you have any records by David Bowie?
notes: « ¿Tienen...? » is a useful neutral Latin American form for asking a shop if they carry something.

lessons.english: Yes, we have several over here.
acceptedTranslations: Yes, we have a few over here.
Yes, we've got several over here.
notes: « Por aquí » is a common way to indicate a nearby area.

lessons.english: Where are the used records?
acceptedTranslations: Where are the secondhand records?
Where can I find the used records?
notes: « Usado » means used or secondhand.

lessons.sentence: Están al fondo, a la izquierda.
lessons.english: They're in the back, on the left.
acceptedTranslations: They're at the back, to the left.
They're in the back on the left.
notes: « Al fondo » is commonly used for something located toward the back of a shop.

lessons.english: Is this record new or used?
acceptedTranslations: Is this a new or used record?
Is this record new or secondhand?
notes: A simple question for checking the condition or category of a record.

lessons.sentence: Es usado, pero está en muy buen estado.
lessons.english: It's used, but it's in very good condition.
acceptedTranslations: It's secondhand, but it's in very good condition.
It's used, but it's in great shape.
notes: « Estar en buen estado » is a useful expression for saying something is in good condition.

lessons.sentence: La portada está un poco dañada.
lessons.english: The cover is a little damaged.
acceptedTranslations: The cover is slightly damaged.
The sleeve is a little damaged.
notes: « La portada » refers to the cover artwork or outer cover.

lessons.english: But the vinyl is fine.
acceptedTranslations: But the record itself is fine.
But the vinyl is in good shape.
notes: « Estar bien » is a simple, common way to say something is okay or in acceptable condition.

lessons.english: Can I listen to it?
acceptedTranslations: May I listen to it?
Can I hear it?
notes: « Lo » refers to the record or album being discussed.

lessons.english: Sure, you can listen to it here.
acceptedTranslations: Of course, you can listen to it here.
Sure, you can play it here.
notes: « Claro » is an extremely common conversational way to say of course or sure.

lessons.english: I love this album.
acceptedTranslations: I really love this album.
I love this record.
notes: « Me encanta » is a common way to express stronger enthusiasm than « me gusta ».

lessons.english: I don't know this record.
acceptedTranslations: I'm not familiar with this record.
I don't know this album.
notes: « Conocer » can mean to be familiar with a person, place, or thing.

lessons.sentence: Si te gusta ese, prueba este.
lessons.english: If you like that one, try this one.
acceptedTranslations: If you like that one, give this one a try.
If you like that, try this.
notes: A natural recommendation from another shopper or someone working in the store.

lessons.english: Can you recommend something similar?
acceptedTranslations: Could you recommend something similar?
Can you recommend something like this?
notes: « ¿Me recomienda...? » is a useful polite way to ask someone for a recommendation.

lessons.sentence: Sí, creo que este te va a gustar.
lessons.english: Yes, I think you're going to like this one.
acceptedTranslations: Yes, I think you'll like this one.
Yes, I think you're going to like this.
notes: « Te va a gustar » is a very common way to say you are going to like something.

lessons.english: How much is this one?
acceptedTranslations: How much does this one cost?
What's the price of this one?
notes: « ¿Cuánto cuesta...? » is one of the most useful shopping constructions.

lessons.english: This one costs twenty dollars.
acceptedTranslations: This one is twenty dollars.
It's twenty dollars.
notes: The currency will naturally vary depending on the country.

lessons.english: It's a little expensive.
acceptedTranslations: It's a bit expensive.
That's a little pricey.
notes: « Un poco + adjective » is a useful pattern for softening a comment.

lessons.english: Okay, I'll take this one.
acceptedTranslations: All right, I'll take this one.
Well, I'll take this one.
notes: « Me llevo este » is a very natural shopping expression meaning that you have decided to buy this one.

lessons.english: Can I pay by card?
acceptedTranslations: Can I pay with a card?
Do you take cards?
notes: A broadly useful question for finishing a purchase.
